"Throughout, a bill rule is the standing rule a user sets up on a bill to catch the transactions that pay it and mark the bill paid, and a bill-rule execution is one application of that rule to one transaction, kept in the records as one row per rule per transaction it was applied to. A bill payment carrying a matched transaction is not an execution and is not counted here, a transaction's own tag to a bill payment is not one either, and an Automation+ automation that moves money is not a bill rule. Count every bill rule and every execution the records hold, whatever its date and whether or not the rule or the execution was later deleted. import re, html
with open('pages_out.txt') as f:

txt = html.unescape(txt)
lines = [re.sub(r' +', ' ', l).strip() for l in txt.splitlines()]
txt = '\n'.join(l for l in lines if l)
